TERRY CUMMINGS.background: Democrat from Mableton (south Cobb County); attorney and retired federal law enforcement officer. Grew up in Teaneck, New Jersey; political science major at Douglass College, Rutgers University, where she led the Douglass Black Student Congress; attended law school at night while working full time; interned for U.S. Sen. Bill Bradley and clerked at D.C. Superior Court. Spent about 25 years with the Federal Bureau of Prisons (entering through the DOJ Honors Attorneys Program), including the Metropolitan Correctional Center in Chicago and the Atlanta Penitentiary, and served on the agency's executive staff before retiring. After retiring she organized returning-citizen job fairs, including for Cobb DA Joyette Holmes's record-restriction event. Post seat holder on the Cobb County Democratic Committee (2020). Lost the June 9, 2020 Democratic primary for House District 39 to incumbent Erica Thomas (34.8%); ran again in 2022 (27.16% in the May primary, heading to a runoff with Monica DeLancy) and has served as the District 39 representative since Jan. 9, 2023.
TERRY CUMMINGS.notes: Rechecked 2026-11-05. She is the sitting Democratic state representative for House District 39 (in office since Jan. 9, 2023, per Wikipedia); her 2022 and later House District 39 races are joined to this profile. State votes/bills left to General Assembly records. The 2022 Cobb Courier story calls Cummings 'he'; the 2020 Courier profile describes her as a wife and mother; she is profiled as female. Wikipedia says born in the Bronx and Georgetown (law) but flags 'citation needed'; the Courier says she grew up in Teaneck, NJ and does not name the law school.

positions.stance: Says the war on drugs failed; many people are imprisoned because of guilty pleas or poor representation; emphasizes jobs for people leaving prison.
Supported HB 346 against landlord retaliation; wants more law-school tenant clinics; would bar landlords from leaving evicted tenants' belongings on the street.
"Sterigenics cannot be trusted to do their own self-reporting"; supported Rep. Erick Allen's and Sen. Jen Jordan's ethylene oxide permitting and monitoring bills and mandatory reporting.
Opposed HB 302, which would bar local design rules for one- and two-family homes: "I don't think that it should be left to the Georgia assembly to just step in."
Praised HB 987 but wanted its training and reporting rules extended to facilities with 25 or fewer beds and longer notice before ownership changes.
Says South Cobb has been left behind and needs investment and sustainable businesses.
Supports initiatives providing veterans quality medical care and assistance.

Priorities include protecting ballot access, strengthening public education, expanding affordable health care, building safer communities, and advancing fairness for families, and will fight to ensure every eligible voter has fair access to the ballot.
q: Her priorities are grounded in protecting access to the ballot, strengthening public education, expanding access to affordable health care, building safer communities, and advancing fairness and opportunity for Georgia families.
As your next representative, I will fight to ensure every eligible voter has fair access to the ballot.

positions.stance: Says Georgia is one of 12 states that has not expanded Medicaid and will expand Medicare for all Georgians, require caps on costly medications, and work on Reproductive Justice Act.
q: Georgia is one of 12 states in our country that has not expanded Medicaid.

As your next Representative, I will diligently work to expand Medicare for all Georgians, require adequate caps on costly medications and therapies, and work on passage of the Reproductive Justice Act to restore abortion options for women.

positions.stance: Will work with stakeholders to ensure leadership is held accountable and is committed to turning people's concerns into practical policies.
q: I will work with stakeholders at the state level to ensure our leadership not only receives the support they need, but they are held accountable for clear expectations and needed improvements.

positions.stance: Would partner with parents and teachers to empower educational leaders.
q: As your next State House Representative, I will partner with parents and teachers to empower our educational leaders with the support, tools, and trust they need to maintain Cobb’s long tradition of excellence in education.

positions.stance: Will ensure guns do not fall in the hands of violent felons, domestic abusers, and those with mental health issues.
q: As your next representative, I will work to ensure guns do not fall in the hands of violent felons, individuals convicted of domestic abuse, and those with a history of serious mental health issues.
